A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 15. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 15.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. 15.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 15.5. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves determination of l u m p s u m a m o u n t s w i t h r e f e r e n c e t o c i r c u m s t a n c e s s u c h a s a g e , n a t u r e o f injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant.

The present accident claim is based on a detailed accident report (Dar) filed by the police in terms of provisions of Mv Act. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 14.01.2020 at around 1 PM, petitioner Anil Jha was going towards Gali No.13, Govindpuri from Govindpuri Metro station on his motorbike bearing no. DL-35DK-4019. Suddenly, an E-Rickshaw bearing no. DL-3ER-1403, driven rashly and negligently by its driver, hit the bike, due to which petitioner fell down and received injuries. He called his company owner and relatives who called PCR and his company vehicle took him to Trauma Center. 3. An FIR no.19/2020 dated 16.01.2020 was registered u/s 279,338 of IPC & 3/181,5/181,146/196 MV Act at PS Govindpuri and the matter was investigated. After investigation, charge sheet was filed before concerned criminal court against the driver of the offending vehicle while DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is driver of offending vehicle and Respondent no.2 is owner of offending vehicle. Offending vehicle (being an E-rickshaw) is uninsured. 5. In response to the DAR, no reply/written statement was filed by Respondents despite opportunity. 6. On the basis of pleadings on record, following issues were framed on 18.12.2021. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 14.01.2020 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL3ER1403 being driven by R1 and owned by CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2024.10.23 16:54:03 +0530 MACT NO:251/21 Anil Jha v. Golu Kumar P.No. 2 Of 17 BK R2? OPP. 3. Relief. 7. Petitioner Anil Jha examined himself as PW-1 and led his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. As per the affidavit, on 14.01.2020 at about 1:00 AM, petitioner was coming on his bike from Govindpuri Metro station and going towards RD Marg near Gate no.13, Govindpuri. While taking a U-turn, an E- rickshaw bearing no. DL-3ER-1403 hit him on his right leg. He was taken AIIMS Trauma Center. He deposed that surgery of his right leg was conducted on 25.01.2019. He was unable to join office for six months. He used to get salary of Rs.21,000/- p.m. He relied upon photographs of E-rickshaw as Ex.PW-1/1, site plan as Ex.PW-1/2, complaint dated 16.01.2020 as Ex.PW-1/3, written complaint dated 16.01.2020 as Ex.PW-1/4, medical documents as Ex.PW-1/5, Anil Jha (Dar) vs Golu Kumar (19/20Gp) on 23 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138723834/ 2 discharge summary as Ex.PW-1/6 and MLC dated 14.01.2020 prepared at AIIMS hospital as Ex.PW- 1/7. He was not cross-examined by respondents despite opportunity. No other witness was examined on behalf of petitioner. Respondents did not lead any evidence. As discussed in issue no.1, petitioner is entitled to compensation.
